theory.intro: For $X \sim \text{Bernoulli}(p)$ the mean is $E(X)=p$ and the variance is $\text{Var}(X)=p(1-p)$. Both come from the discrete formulas $E(X)=\sum xP(x)$ and $\text{Var}(X)=\sum x^2P(x)-[E(X)]^2$. The standard deviation is $\sigma(X)=\sqrt{p(1-p)}$.
facts: $E(X)=p$: the mean of a Bernoulli variable is simply its probability of success.
$E(X)=0(1-p)+1(p)=p$, because only the value $x=1$ contributes to the sum.
$\text{Var}(X)=p(1-p)$ may also be written $pq$, where $q=1-p$ is the probability of failure.
$\sigma(X)=\sqrt{p(1-p)}$ is the standard deviation of a Bernoulli variable.
The variance is greatest when $p=0.5$, where $\text{Var}(X)=0.25$, and it is never larger than that.
The variance is $0$ when $p=0$ or $p=1$, because the result of the trial is then certain.
The mean $p$ is not a value $X$ can take unless $p$ is $0$ or $1$.
steps: Write down $p$, the probability of success.
Take the square root of the variance if the standard deviation is asked for.

foundation.question_text: A biased coin shows heads with probability $0.25$. Let $X=1$ if the coin shows heads. Find the mean and the variance of $X$.
$X \sim \text{Bernoulli}(0.7)$. Find $\sigma(X)$, correct to three decimal places.

The table shows a Bernoulli distribution.
$\begin{array}{c|cc} x & 0 & 1 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.55 & 0.45 \end{array}$
Use $E(X)=\sum xP(x)$ and $\text{Var}(X)=\sum x^2P(x)-[E(X)]^2$ to find $E(X)$ and $\text{Var}(X)$.
$X$ is a Bernoulli random variable with $E(X)=0.62$. Find $\text{Var}(X)$.
A seed germinates with probability $0.8$, and $X=1$ if the seed germinates. Find $E(X)$, $\text{Var}(X)$ and $\sigma(X)$.

development.question_text: A Bernoulli random variable has $\text{Var}(X)=0.16$ and $p<0.5$. Find $p$.
A Bernoulli random variable has $\sigma(X)=0.3$ and $p>0.5$. Find $p$.
For $X \sim \text{Bernoulli}(p)$, find the value of $p$ that makes $\text{Var}(X)$ greatest, and state that greatest variance.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Var}(X)=p(1-p)$
$=p-p^2$
This is a concave parabola in $p$ with zeros at $p=0$ and $p=1$, so it peaks midway between them.
$p=0.5$
$\text{Var}(X)=0.5(0.5)$
$=0.25$

development.question_text:
A Bernoulli distribution is given below.
$\begin{array}{c|cc} x & 0 & 1 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.88 & 0.12 \end{array}$
Find $\sum x^2P(x)$ and hence $\text{Var}(X)$.
In a factory $18\%$ of tiles are chipped. One tile is chosen and $X=1$ if the tile is chipped. Find $E(X)$ and $\text{Var}(X)$.
A train is on time with probability $0.95$. Let $X=1$ if the train is **late**. Find the mean and the variance of $X$.
One Bernoulli variable has $p=0.3$ and another has $p=0.45$. Which has the greater standard deviation? Justify your answer.

The variable with $p=0.45$ has the greater standard deviation, because $p(1-p)$ grows as $p$ moves closer to $0.5$.

development.question_text: A Bernoulli random variable satisfies $\text{Var}(X)=0.24E(X)$, where $p \ne 0$. Find $p$.

A Bernoulli distribution is given below.
$\begin{array}{c|cc} x & 0 & 1 \\ \hline P(X=x) & \frac{3}{5} & \frac{2}{5} \end{array}$
Find $E(X)$ and $\text{Var}(X)$ as fractions.

mastery.question_text: For a Bernoulli random variable, $E(X)+\text{Var}(X)=0.96$. Find $p$.
Show that $\text{Var}(X)=0.25-(p-0.5)^2$ for a Bernoulli random variable, and hence explain why $\text{Var}(X)$ can never exceed $0.25$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Var}(X)=p(1-p)$
$=p-p^2$
$=-(p^2-p)$
$=-\left((p-0.5)^2-0.25\right)$
$=0.25-(p-0.5)^2$
Since $(p-0.5)^2 \ge 0$, the term subtracted is never negative, so $\text{Var}(X) \le 0.25$ with equality only at $p=0.5$.

mastery.question_text: A quiz item is answered correctly by a randomly chosen student with probability $p$. The Bernoulli variable for one student has $\text{Var}(X)=0.2464$. Find the two possible values of $p$.
